title: A read-only run cannot clone: the factory's git door refuses the run's own credential
description:
Found by the Phase 4 closeout's live check — the first unattended loop this epic ever ran against the deployed factory, which is exactly what the epic's definition of done asks for.

PR #58 was opened; the author-trust gate admitted it (pull_request/opened -> 202) and run_19cb914ba6484ac59847f0e85f680712 was dispatched for epic pr-58 with nobody in the loop. It then failed in 28 seconds:

  ticks-orchestrator: the remote refused a shallow fetch of the SHA; fetching history
  fatal: Authentication failed for 'https://ticks-factory.pe-1a0.workers.dev/api/git/pengelbrecht/ticks.git/'
  ticks-orchestrator: cannot fetch https://ticks-factory.pe-1a0.workers.dev/api/git/pengelbrecht/ticks.git

EVERYTHING ELSE IN THE EPIC WORKED, which is what makes this precise rather than vague:
- the loop dispatched unattended;
- tick pzf's design held — the run was given the factory-mediated remote (/api/git/...) instead of GitHub, which is the whole point of the read-only grade;
- tick acy's 'tk cloud supervisor' answered from OUTSIDE the supervisor on the first try (status complete, 8 steps, timings);
- tick hyi's trace id is on the log line (ticks-trace: tr_8d7eb4ee...).

So the credential DESIGN is right and the DOOR is broken: a read-only run holds a tkr_ token and the git proxy will not accept it. Two shapes to check, and the evidence does not yet distinguish them — say which it was:
1. The proxy does not implement the auth scheme git actually sends. Git uses HTTP Basic over the credential; if the route expects a bearer header it never sees one, and 'Authentication failed' is git reporting a 401 it could not satisfy.
2. The token is not reaching git at all — no credential helper, no askpass, nothing in the URL — so git authenticates anonymously and is refused.

Note the line above the failure: 'the remote refused a shallow fetch of the SHA; fetching history'. The proxy answered SOMETHING for the initial probe, so it is reachable and partially functional; the failure is on the authenticated fetch.

This is the last thing between Phase 4 and its definition of done — no loop has yet run unattended end to end, because this one cannot get the code.

Also fixed the thing that was hitting the operator: an early iteration of git_door_test.go spawned a real git that fell through to the host's credential-osxkeychain and prompted them to create a keychain, repeatedly. The committed test isolates HOME, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and GIT_ASKPASS — and asserts its own source contains those, so a future test cannot omit them silently. Verified: internal/sandbox runs clean with no prompt.
acceptance_criteria: A read-only run clones through the factory's git door using its own run credential and completes its review; proven by an unattended live run that leaves a review comment, not by a unit test.
closed_reason: Completed: the factory's git door now sends a WWW-Authenticate challenge on 401, so git offers its Basic credential. Shape 1 of the two candidates — the token was in the container all along; the door's 401s were bare Response.json bodies with no challenge, and git will not volunteer a credential it was never asked for. Diagnosed from a real unattended run rather than guessed.
